theme.vibe: A calm pond at dusk with springy shapes, soft ripples, and leafy places to perch.
theme.decorativeMotif: Lily pads, pond ripples, reeds, and curved hop paths that make pages feel bouncy and alive.

cover.title: Frogs Hop, Swim, and Grow
cover.subtitle: A pond-to-tree look at frog life

pages.text: Frogs are amphibians. Many have big eyes and strong back legs.
extras: Adult frogs do not have tails.

images.alt: A red-eyed leaf frog resting on a bright green leaf.

pages.layoutHint: Opening portrait page with one large frog and roomy text, like a frog pausing on a lily pad.

pages.text: Many frogs jump. Many can swim too. They often stay near fresh water or other damp places.
extras: Frogs live in many places around the world.

images.alt: A close-up of an American green tree frog.
A gray tree frog resting on rough tree bark.

pages.layoutHint: Two-photo spread with a gentle curve between images, suggesting a hop from one perch to another.

pages.text: Some frogs live in trees. Tree frogs often have sticky toe pads that help them hold on.
extras: Frog skin can be smooth, bumpy, bright, or camouflaged.

images.alt: A European tree frog clinging to a plant stem.
An American green tree frog seen close up on a perch.

pages.layoutHint: Vertical climbing layout with text tucked beside the frogs, as if rising through reeds and branches.

pages.text: Frogs make calls. Adult frogs often eat small animals such as insects.
extras: Frogs make many calls during breeding season.

images.alt: A red-eyed leaf frog posed on a leaf, ready to call.

pages.layoutHint: Low-text page with ripples or sound-wave styling around a single frog portrait.

pages.text: Many frogs lay their eggs in water. Frog eggs are often called frogspawn.
extras: The life cycle begins in water for many frogs.

images.alt: Clear frogspawn floating in shallow water.

pages.layoutHint: Wide, airy pond page with plenty of space around the egg clusters.

pages.text: The eggs hatch into tadpoles. Tadpoles live in water and have tails for swimming.
extras: As tadpoles grow, they begin to grow legs.

images.alt: A common frog tadpole in the water just before metamorphosis.

pages.layoutHint: Underwater-feeling page with the text flowing along a tail-like curve.

pages.text: A tadpole changes into a frog in metamorphosis. The tail shrinks, and lungs develop.
extras: This big change happens as the young frog grows.

images.alt: A tadpole with a tail, showing the water stage of frog life.
A tree frog showing the later stage after metamorphosis.

pages.layoutHint: Before-and-after comparison spread with a clear left-to-right growth path.

pages.text: There are thousands of frog species. Some are tiny, and some are much bigger.
extras: Some frogs use bright colors to warn other animals to leave them alone.

images.alt: A colorful red-eyed leaf frog on a leaf.
A gray tree frog blending in against bark.

pages.layoutHint: Comparison page pairing a bright frog with a camouflaged frog to show variety.

pages.text: Frogs are an important part of food webs. Many frog species are in trouble and need safe places to live.
extras: Wet places, ponds, and forests can help frogs.

images.alt: An American green tree frog looking out from a green perch.
Frogspawn in shallow water, showing one stage that needs a safe habitat.

pages.layoutHint: Gentle closing spread with a protective pond feeling and space for a hopeful ending.

backMatter.notes: Theme direction: rounded headings, calm body text, pond-ripple spacing, and lily-pad or reed accents to give this frog book its own springy rhythm.
